core_contrarian_theses.conventional_myth: Hire your wealth and tax planning team right after you sign the Letter of Intent to sell your company.
core_contrarian_theses.client_conviction: Waiting until a binding LOI is signed locks you out of the highest-impact pre-exit estate, trust, and charitable gifting structures.
core_contrarian_theses.proof_mechanism: Under the IRS anticipatory assignment of income doctrine, transferring shares after a deal is substantially certain can trigger immediate tax recognition.

core_contrarian_theses.conventional_myth: Holding 70% of your net worth in employer RSUs after vesting is 'staying loyal' or 'waiting for the stock to bounce back'.

core_contrarian_theses.proof_mechanism: RSUs are taxed as ordinary W-2 income on the day they vest—there is zero long-term capital gains benefit to holding newly vested shares.

few_shot_calibration.raw_async_voice_transcript_snippet: Uh recording this between client reviews—one thing that breaks my heart in pre-exit work is getting an urgent phone call where a founder says 'David we signed our binding alloy yesterday, how do we reduce taxes before closing?' Sequence and calendar dates matter more than cleverness. Once a binding L O I is signed and deal terms are substantially locked, IRS rules around anticipatory assignment of income shut down most charitable remainder trusts, family trust share gifts at pre-deal valuations, or fixing broken Q S B S paperwork without triggering immediate tax recognition. Founders who keep the highest share of net proceeds coordinate their CPA, M&A counsel, and fiduciary planner 12 to 24 months before going to market—auditing C-corp structure, completing family transfers before formal bids, and modeling post-exit cash flow. Make sure compliance disclaimer is on this.
few_shot_calibration.generic_ai_slop_version: Selling your business? Unlock massive tax loopholes and skyrocket your wealth with our seamless secret strategies! Don't leave free money on the table! 🚀 #Wealth #Exit
few_shot_calibration.authentic_client_gold_version:
The costliest pre-exit phone call starts with: "We signed our LOI—how do we reduce taxes before closing?"

Sequence and calendar dates matter more than cleverness. Once a binding LOI is signed and deal terms are substantially locked, IRS rules around anticipatory assignment of income narrow your options dramatically.

Charitable remainder trusts, gifting shares to family trusts at pre-deal valuations, or fixing broken QSBS (Section 1202) documentation often become ineffective or trigger immediate tax recognition.

Founders who keep the highest share of net proceeds coordinate their CPA, M&A counsel, and fiduciary planner 12 to 24 months before going to market:
• Auditing C-corp vs. S-corp structure and 5-year QSBS clocks early
• Completing family or charitable share transfers prior to formal buyer bids
• Modeling post-exit cash flow needs before negotiating earnout terms

Bring your planning team to the table before the investment banker launches the process. Educational commentary only; not individualized investment, tax, or legal advice.

few_shot_calibration.topic_context: Helping senior tech leaders reframe newly vested RSUs.
few_shot_calibration.raw_async_voice_transcript_snippet: Um quick thought on R S U vesting schedules—so many senior engineering VPs sit on $2M plus of vested employer shares because selling feels disloyal or they think they should wait a year for long-term capital gains. Here is why timing matters on vesting day: unlike incentive stock options, R S U shares are taxed as ordinary W-2 cash income the exact morning they vest, and your cost basis resets to that day's market price. Holding newly vested shares gives you zero tax discount on the grant itself, while tying both your paycheck and your retirement balance sheet to a single ticker. Ask yourself one clarifying question on every quarterly vest date: if the company wired you $150,000 in after-tax cash today, would you log into your brokerage account and spend 100% of it buying more company shares? Make sure compliance disclaimer is on this.
few_shot_calibration.generic_ai_slop_version: Holding company stock is risky! Beat the market effortlessly with our guaranteed diversification playbook!
few_shot_calibration.authentic_client_gold_version:
Many VPs sit on $2M+ of vested employer RSUs because selling feels disloyal—or they assume waiting cuts the grant tax.

Here is why timing matters on vesting day.

Unlike incentive stock options, RSUs are taxed as ordinary W-2 income the moment shares vest. Your cost basis resets to that morning's market price. Holding newly vested shares ties both your career income and family balance sheet to a single stock without lowering the vest-day tax bill.

Ask one clarifying question on every quarterly vest date: "If the company wired me $150,000 in after-tax cash today, would I log into my brokerage account and spend 100% of it buying more company shares?"

If the answer is no, automating a structured sell-to-diversify calendar rule removes emotion from the decision. Educational commentary only; not individualized investment, tax, or legal advice.
